summary: Ephemeral healthcheck flapping causing attach thundering and dedicated pool degradation
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 14:05 UTC GridForms reported sustained p99/p50 latency increases and intermittent attach failures for requests routed to their dedicated pool. Impact: customer requests see 10-30s attach delays and ~6% 5xx rate for short-lived streams; overall throughput for the reserved pool dropped ~28% during the window. Environment: dedicated pool (reserve-id: gforms-prod-west), prod, us-west-2, model redwood-3b-v2. Observed behavior: periodic bursts of ephemeral healthcheck connections from tenant sidecars (aligned with heartbeat jitter) appear to throttle allocator attach operations, triggering parallel attach retries and a thundering attach pattern that starves batchers and stalls prefetch. Expected behavior: healthchecks should be rate-limited and not interfere with attach/slot allocation; allocator should queue and throttle without cascading client-side retries.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Target the customer's dedicated endpoint with many short-lived streams (1-5s inference) from multiple client hosts.
2) Introduce jittered healthcheck probes from a sidecar process every 5-15s across hosts (simulate ephemeral flapping).
3) Observe allocator attach latencies, prefetch queue depth, and batcher slot utilization in the reserved pool dashboard.
4) Compare with baseline where healthchecks are disabled or strictly rate-limited.
impact: Customer-facing latency regression: p50 increased from ~120ms to 1.1s, p99 spiked to 11s. Throughput dropped by ~28% for the dedicated pool during peak of the event. Several production tenants on the same physical cluster experienced head-of-line effects until autoscaler rebalanced. Business impact: GridForms reports user-facing timeouts and automated failover triggers in their app; revenue-affecting incidents if not resolved.
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Ayesha): correlated increased attach latency with a rise in short TCP connections from customer's sidecars around 14:00 UTC; snapshotter IO and prefetch metrics remained nominal.

SRE (Liam): allocator logs show attach request queue growth and attach-retry storms (attach attempts per slot > 12/min) during the window. Kernel-level traces show rapid connect/close cycles causing NVMe io random writes, but not full saturation.

Hypothesis: jittered healthcheck probes from the customer's sidecar are creating ephemeral TCP sessions that coincide with attach scheduling. Client-side retry/backoff absent -> simultaneous attach attempts cause the allocator to escalate allocation, which interacts poorly with batcher windowing and triggers slot starvation.

Telemetry: increased small-stream fanout metric + elevated attach_retries_count. Prefetch lease churn increased 3x. Autoscaler attempted to add nodes but cool-down settings delayed effective capacity expansion, prolonging impact.
Cross-reference: similar symptom pattern to SUP-314159 but root cause there was background snapshotter noise; here the dominant signal is ephemeral healthcheck flapping from tenant sidecars.
comments: 2026-03-10 15:02 - Support (Ayesha): Reached out to GridForms to confirm any recent sidecar or agent upgrades. Asked for their sidecar config and samples of healthcheck timing.
2026-03-10 15:37 - GridForms (customer): Confirmed a rollout of a new monitoring agent at 13:50 UTC which added fast liveness checks; provided sidecar logs showing probes every 7-12s from ~30 hosts.

2026-03-10 16:10 - SRE (Liam): Deployed temporary rate-limit on attach requests at the allocator edge for the affected pool to dampen thundering. Early telemetry shows attach retries drop by ~65% and p99 latency receding.
2026-03-11 09:20 - Support (Ayesha): Advised GridForms to patch sidecar to exponential backoff on probe retries and to enable randomized healthcheck offsets; provided a recommended delta config.

2026-03-12 11:05 - SRE (Liam): Working on a safer allocator backpressure strategy and a circuit-breaker for ephemeral-connection storms; opened PR to add attach-rate limiter and jitter-aware scheduling.
resolution: Workaround applied: edge-level attach rate limiting for the affected dedicated pool reduced attach storms and restored throughput to ~92% of baseline within 40 minutes of deployment.

Customer mitigation: GridForms rolled back the monitoring agent and patched their sidecar to add randomized probe offsets and a 2-8s exponential backoff; confirmed on 2026-03-11 that their retries stopped correlating with attach spikes.

Long-term actions: (1) Implement allocator attach-rate limiter and jitter-aware scheduling (PR referenced). (2) Update dedicated-pool runbook with guidance for tenant-side healthchecks and recommended rate limits. (3) Add autoscaler cooldown tuning for rapid short-lived fanouts to reduce delayed capacity response.
